message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way to spin up a VM) and also shows the equivalent **REST API** call if you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the **gcloud CLI** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have the **GPU driver** installed on the instance after it boots (see the “Post‑boot steps” section).  
> * The **GPU quota** for your project is sufficient (at least one RTX A6000).  

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to suit your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count="$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | 100 GB SSD boot disk. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional script that runs on first boot (see below). |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU driver installation). |
| `--tags` | Opens HTTP/HTTPS ports if you want to expose a web service. |

#### Optional: Startup script to install NVIDIA drivers

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver and CUDA (required for GPU usage)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the instance boots, the script will install the driver and reboot automatically.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (HTTP)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), use the following POST request.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token (`<YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>`) with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

---

## 3. Post‑boot steps (if you didn’t use a startup script)

After the instance is running, SSH into it and install the NVIDIA driver manually:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=$PROJECT --zone=$ZONE

# Update package lists
sudo apt-get update

# Install the driver (replace 535 with the latest driver version if needed)
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to load the driver
sudo reboot
```

Once the instance reboots, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 4. Quick sanity check

```bash
# List instances to confirm creation
gcloud compute instances list --project=$PROJECT --zone=$ZONE

# Verify GPU
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=$PROJECT --zone=$ZONE --command="nvidia-smi"
```

If `nvidia-smi` shows the RTX A6000, everything is set up correctly.

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

That single command (plus the optional `startup.sh`) will give you a fully‑functional Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for deep‑learning, rendering, or any GPU‑heavy workload.
